title: The Clinical Reasoning Framework
lead: Every later chapter uses the same eight steps.

blocks.text: Every later chapter uses the same eight steps. If you learn them here, you can follow any condition chapter in this book.

rows: Something you see, measure or the patient tells you
A finding that makes one diagnosis more or less likely
The best explanation for all the findings so far
A diagnosis proven by the accepted diagnostic process (often medical testing)
Another condition that could explain the same presentation
A warning finding that needs a safety action
A reason your examination cannot settle the diagnosis

items: **Screen** for serious conditions before routine treatment.
**Examine** with tests chosen for this patient, not a routine battery.
**Interpret** all findings together, not one test alone.
**Choose** the next action: treat, assess more, investigate, or refer.
**Plan** management: preferred start, reason, alternatives, progression.

blocks.text: At each step, write one decision sentence: Because the patient has finding A and no contraindication, I will do X. If finding B appears, I will not do X; I will do Z.

rows: Possible threat to life or major function (for example rapidly progressing weakness, new bladder or bowel loss with saddle numbness, chest pain with autonomic symptoms)
Stop the session. Arrange emergency transfer or call emergency services
Serious cause possible but patient stable (for example unexplained weight loss with night pain)
Defer treatment. Same-day or within-days physician review. Document
Needs another specialist's opinion but is not time-critical
Continue safe care. Refer through usual pathway

blocks.text: A single red flag does **not** confirm a disease. It tells you to look harder and act safely.
If a test reproduces the patient's pain, it shows that the tested region is sensitive. It does not prove a specific structural lesion. This rule applies to every special test in this book.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Define finding, clue, working diagnosis and red flag in your own words.
Name the eight steps in order.
Choose between emergency, urgent and routine action for a described patient.
